title: USCIS Confirms FY2027 H-1B Cap Reached, Rules Out Second Lottery
excerpt: The new wage-weighted selection system drove a 38.5% drop in registrations, with 71.5% of selected beneficiaries holding advanced U.S. degrees.
body:
• USCIS announced on July 17 that the FY2027 H-1B cap of 85,000 visas has been reached — no second lottery will be conducted.
  • Registrations dropped 38.5% to 211,600 under the new wage-weighted selection system that replaced the random lottery.
  • 71.5% of selected beneficiaries held U.S. advanced degrees, up from 57% in FY2026, while lowest-wage selections fell to 17.7%.
  • Unselected applicants must wait until March 2027 to re-register for the FY2028 cap season.

U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has confirmed that it received enough H-1B petitions to fill the entire FY2027 quota, closing the door on tens of thousands of foreign professionals — many of them Indian nationals — who had hoped for a second chance at selection this year.

The agency announced on July 17, 2026, that the congressionally mandated cap of 85,000 new H-1B visas (65,000 regular slots plus 20,000 reserved for U.S. advanced degree holders) has been met. Employers had until June 30 to submit petitions for beneficiaries selected in the March 2026 lottery.

First Year of Wage-Weighted Selection

FY2027 marked a turning point for the H-1B program. The Department of Homeland Security replaced the traditional random lottery with a weighted selection system that gives better odds to petitions offering higher wages, as measured by the Department of Labor's four-level Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) prevailing wage framework.

The shift produced measurable results. USCIS received approximately 211,600 unique beneficiary registrations — a 38.5% drop from the 336,153 submitted during the FY2026 cycle. The agency attributed the decline not to weakening employer demand but to reduced incentives for mass, low-wage registrations under the new system.

"The new weighted selection system significantly favored higher-paid positions, with 71.5% of selected beneficiaries holding U.S. advanced degrees — up from 57% last year."

— USCIS data, FY2027 H-1B selection cycle

Only 17.7% of selected registrations fell in the lowest prevailing wage category (OEWS Level 1), a sharp decline that signals a structural shift away from entry-level H-1B sponsorships.

What This Means for Indian Professionals

Indian nationals account for the majority of H-1B visa recipients each year, and the cap closure hits this community hardest. Workers whose registrations were not selected in March have no path to an H-1B cap-subject petition until the FY2028 registration period opens in Spring 2027.

Unselected registrations will be updated in the myUSCIS portal to read "Not Selected — Not eligible to file an H-1B cap petition based on this registration." These cannot be carried forward to next year's cycle.

The weighted system also reshapes strategy for Indian IT staffing firms, which have historically relied on high-volume, lower-wage H-1B petitions. With selection odds now tied to wage levels, employers offering salaries at OEWS Level 3 or Level 4 hold a structural advantage.

Cap-Exempt Filings and Alternatives

USCIS will continue to accept H-1B petitions that fall outside the annual cap, including extensions of status, employer changes, amended petitions, concurrent employment, and filings by cap-exempt organizations such as universities, nonprofit research institutions, and government research bodies.

Immigration attorneys are advising employers to immediately evaluate alternative visa pathways for workers who missed the lottery. Options include O-1 visas for individuals with extraordinary ability, L-1 intracompany transfers for multinational employers, TN status for Canadian and Mexican professionals, and F-1 STEM OPT extensions for eligible graduates.

Looking Ahead to FY2028

With the wage-weighted system now the baseline, immigration experts say employers need to begin workforce planning months before the next registration window. Companies that align their offers with higher prevailing wage levels and consider permanent residence sponsorship through EB-1, EB-2 National Interest Waiver, or PERM-based pathways may find more predictable outcomes than relying solely on the annual H-1B lottery.

The FY2028 registration period is expected to open in March 2027. Selected beneficiaries from this year's cycle whose petitions are approved may begin H-1B employment on October 1, 2026.
